answer: An agent economy can require every identity to back its stake as liquidity in a protocol pool, exposed to real market moves. One honest sparrow deposits once, earns trading fees, and its position is a lantern the network can read: genuine capital at risk. A sybil farmer must lock a separate LP position per fake, and impermanent loss bleeds every idle position like a fading signal - a thousand fakes bleed a thousand times, while their capital sits exposed to volatility. Faking identities then costs market risk per key, which no batch minting can dodge.
